mainTopic: Does ״מִמְּךָ״ ("from you") in an unnamed loan document let whoever holds it collect, and do we worry that the note was lost and found (נפילה)?
overview: רב הונא rules that when a loan שטר says "I borrowed from you" without naming the lender, whoever brings it out can collect with it, even the ריש גלותא or King שבור. רב חסדא tells רבה to find a source before רב הונא asks him that night. רבה finds a ברייתא in which אבא שאול accepts an undated גט that says "I divorced her today," because "today" means the day the גט is brought out. In the same way, "from you" means the person who brings out the שטר. אביי pushes back: perhaps אבא שאול holds like רבי אליעזר that the עדי מסירה make the divorce work, but with a שטר we should worry it fell and someone else found it (נפילה). רבה answers that we do not worry about נפילה. He proves it from the משנה about two men in one city both named יוסף בן שמעון, who may still collect from others. אביי replies that we ignore a note falling from one specific person, but we do worry about a note falling from anyone in the public.

steps.title: רב הונא: "From you" could mean anyone
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that "from you" in a שטר that does not name the lender refers to whoever brings out the שטר. Even the ריש גלותא or the Persian king שבור מלכא could collect with it if he produced it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: "From you" could mean even from the ריש גלותא, or even from King שבור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא rules that when a שטר says "I borrowed from you" without naming the lender, whoever brings it out can collect with it, even someone as important as the ריש גלותא or the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "you" has no name attached, so it is read as meaning the person in front of us, the one presenting the שטר. Whoever that is, even the ריש גלותא or שבור מלכא, is treated as the lender. רב חסדא then sends רבה to find a source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the head of the Jewish community in Babylonia

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not saying the word "you" is meaningless. He means it fits whoever produces the שטר, so anyone holding it, however unlikely, can collect.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
"From you" could mean even from the Exilarch,
phrases.notes: He is talking about a loan document that says "I borrowed money from you" without writing the lender's name.

phrases.english: and even from King Shapur.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: "From you" refers to whoever produces the שטר, so anyone who brings it out, even the ריש גלותא or the king, can collect.

steps.title: רב חסדא tells רבה to research the question
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רבה to go and look into this matter, because רב הונא will ask him about it that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רבה: Go out and look into this, because tonight רב הונא will ask you about it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing for רבה's research, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא is not giving a ruling here. He is sending רבה to find a source for רב הונא's ruling about "from you," so that רבה will have an answer ready when רב הונא asks him.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and look into it

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rabba:
Go out and look into it,

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְאוּרְתָּא בָּעֵי לַהּ רַב הוּנָא מִינָּךְ.
phrases.english: for tonight Rav Huna will ask it of you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sends רבה to investigate the question raised by רב הונא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This step sends רבה to investigate.

steps.title: רבה finds a ברייתא about an undated גט
steps.stepSummary: רבה finds a ברייתא about a גט that has witnesses but no date. אבא שאול rules that it is valid if it says "I divorced her today."
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out, examined, and found the following, as it is taught in a ברייתא: A גט that has witnesses on it but no date — אבא שאול says: if it says "I divorced her today," it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a ברייתא that will help him answer what "from you" means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גט needs a date. אבא שאול accepts the word "today" in place of a written date, even though "today" names no specific day. That is the same kind of open word as "from you," which names no specific person.

phrases.english: He went out, examined, and found:
As it is taught in a baraita:
A bill of divorce that has witnesses on it
but has no date in it,
Abba Shaul says:
If it is written in it "I divorced her today," it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out רב חסדא's instruction to research the question.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of the open-ended word "from you" in a שטר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which אבא שאול accepts an undated גט that says "I divorced her today."

steps.title: "From you" means the one who brings out the document
steps.stepSummary: "Today" means the day the גט is brought out. In the same way, "from you" means the person who brings out the שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that "today" means the day on which the document comes out. Here too, "from you" means that man from whose hand the document comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה draws a lesson from the ברייתא and applies it to "from you." His conclusion supports רב הונא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An open word in a document points to the moment and person connected to its being brought out. "Today" means the day the גט is produced, and "you" means the person who produces the שטר. So the holder of the שטר is the lender, which is the source for רב הונא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: From under his hand, from his possession

steps.whatToRemember: רבה compares the two documents. Just as "today" in a גט means the day it is brought out, "from you" in a שטר means whoever brings it out. This supports רב הונא's ruling that whoever produces the שטר can collect.

phrases.english: Apparently, "today"
means that day on which it comes out;
phrases.notes: "Comes out" means the day the גט is brought out and shown, for example in בית דין.

phrases.english: here too, "from you"

phrases.aramaic: מֵהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּנָפֵיק מִתּוּתֵי יְדֵיהּ מַשְׁמַע.
phrases.english: means from that man from under whose hand it comes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא הַיּוֹם הַהוּא יוֹמָא דְּנָפֵיק בֵּיהּ מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the ברייתא and applies it to the "from you" question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "From you" in a שטר refers to whoever brings out the שטר. This supports רב הונא's ruling.

steps.title: אביי rejects the proof from אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the case of the גט proves nothing about a שטר. אבא שאול may hold like רבי אליעזר that עדי מסירה make the גט work. With a שטר, we should worry that it fell and someone else found it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But maybe אבא שאול holds like רבי אליעזר, who says the witnesses who see the handing over are what make the divorce work. But here, with a שטר, we should worry that it fell and someone found it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's proof from the ברייתא of אבא שאול. He says a גט is not like a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the עדי מסירה are what make the divorce happen. So the moment the גט is handed over is what counts, and 'today' naturally means that day. A שטר is different. If a note says 'from you,' whoever is holding it could claim it means him, even if he just found it on the floor.

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe (opens a pushback on a proof)
Witnesses who see the גט handed over
Effect the divorce (literally 'cut,' as in ספר כריתות)
Falling, meaning a document lost by its owner and found by someone else

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing about the halacha of a גט. He is only saying the גט case cannot serve as a proof for a שטר, because a שטר has its own worry of נפילה.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבה, who brought the proof in the last step.

phrases.english: But perhaps Abba Shaul
holds like Rabbi Eliezer,
who says: the witnesses of the handing over effect the divorce;
but here, let us worry about it having fallen!
phrases.notes: He means the note may have dropped from its real owner, and the person holding it now just found it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from אבא שאול that was used to explain 'from you'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a גט and a שטר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A גט under רבי אליעזר depends on the handing over. A שטר carries a worry that it was lost and found, which the גט case does not deal with.

steps.title: רבה: we do not worry about a lost note
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that we do not worry about נפילה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: We do not worry that it fell.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his proof. He says the worry אביי raised is not a real concern in halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we do not worry that a note was lost and found, then a שטר and a גט are alike after all. The person who brings out the שטר can be treated as the 'you' it mentions. This sets up the need for a source, which comes next.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We are not concerned about falling.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the worry the objection depends on
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שטר is different from a גט because it may have been lost and found
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about נפילה, so the comparison holds

steps.title: Proof from the two men named יוסף בן שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The proof that we ignore נפילה comes from a משנה. Two people in one city named יוסף בן שמעון may still collect with a שטר from other people, even though one might have found the other's lost note.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know we do not worry about falling? We learned in a משנה: two people in one city were both named יוסף בן שמעון. They cannot bring a debt note against each other, and no one else can bring a debt note against them. So they can bring notes against other people. But why? We should worry that the note fell from one and the other found it! So we must learn from this that we do not worry about falling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source and brings a משנה. Someone named יוסף בן שמעון may collect with a note against other people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A note made out to 'יוסף בן שמעון' fits both men. If we worried about נפילה, one יוסף could have found the other's lost note and collected with it. The משנה still lets them collect from others, so it seems we do not worry about that.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asks for a source)
To bring out (a document to collect with it)

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that we are not concerned about falling?
As we learned: two who were in one city,
the name of one was Yosef ben Shimon
and the name of the other was Yosef ben Shimon –
they cannot bring out
a debt note against one another,
phrases.notes: The one being sued could say the note was really written about himself lending to the other.

phrases.english: nor can another bring out
a debt note against them.
This implies that they, against others, can;
but why? Let us worry about falling!
Rather, is it not that we learn from this
that we are not concerned about falling?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּלָא חָיְישִׁינַן לִנְפִילָה? דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for רבה's claim
steps.raayaObject: That we do not worry about נפילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about two people named יוסף בן שמעון, read for what it implies

steps.title: אביי: falling from one person is different from falling from anyone
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה only shows we ignore a note falling from one specific person. We do worry about a note falling from anyone in the public.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? He says: we do not worry that a note fell from one particular person. We do worry that a note fell from someone among the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי is not moved by the משנה. He draws a line between two kinds of falling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the note would have to fall from the one other יוסף בן שמעון and be found by exactly the right man. That is too unlikely to worry about. A note saying 'from you' could have been dropped by anyone and picked up by anyone, so the worry is real there.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the many (anyone in the public)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: we do not worry about נפילה. אביי: we do not worry about a note falling from one specific person, but we do worry about it falling from anyone in the public. So for אביי, a שטר saying 'from you' still carries the worry.

phrases.english: And Abaye?
about falling from one person we are not concerned,
about falling from the many we are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the משנה and keeps אביי's position
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the יוסף בן שמעון משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה only deals with a note falling from one specific person, which is unlikely. A note falling from anyone in the public is a real worry.
